description: We’re looking for creative, curious, and motivated people who are excited about space, technology, science, design, or simply trying something new. Our challenge is the “Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map,” and we’re aiming to build something innovative, useful, and fun.
summary:
**MarsWalk AI Navigator – AI-Powered Mars Exploration & Safe Return System**

MarsWalk AI Navigator is an intelligent mission-planning prototype designed to make future Mars exploration safer, smarter, and more efficient.

Our project combines an interactive Mars map, AI-inspired decision-making, route optimization, and a simulated smart helmet Heads-Up Display (HUD) to support astronaut exploration.

The system evaluates scientific destinations based on scientific value, accessibility, terrain-related risks, and available mission time. Using Dijkstra's algorithm, our Java-based planner calculates optimal routes and estimates travel time.

A safe-return assessment considers outbound travel, exploration time, return travel, and an additional safety buffer. The system recommends a feasible destination and explains its decision.

Built with Java, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, the prototype connects a mission-planning API to an interactive web application.

Our current model uses experimental route data, with future plans to integrate validated NASA terrain datasets and more advanced navigation capabilities.

Our mission is to help future astronauts explore farther, make smarter decisions, and return safely.
details:
MarsWalk AI Navigator is an intelligent Mars exploration and mission-planning prototype designed to support safer and more efficient astronaut missions.

Our web application combines an interactive Mars map, AI-inspired mission planning, route optimization, and a simulated smart helmet Heads-Up Display (HUD).

Astronauts can enter their available mission time, and the system evaluates exploration sites based on scientific value, accessibility, travel time, and terrain-related risks. Using Dijkstra's algorithm, our Java-based planner calculates optimized routes and checks whether astronauts have enough time to explore and safely return to base, including a safety buffer.

We developed the project using Java, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and REST APIs, with VS Code, GitHub, GitHub Pages, and Render.

Our innovation is integrating scientific priorities, navigation, time management, and safety considerations into one interactive platform.

Our goal is to demonstrate how intelligent decision-support technology could improve future Mars exploration. The current prototype uses illustrative terrain data, with future plans to integrate validated NASA datasets and advanced navigation capabilities.
